title: San Antonio’s Centro de Artes Celebrates 10 Years with "Mercado/Material"
summary: Curated by Mia Lopez, 16 artists transform everyday objects into bold explorations of Latinx identity. On view in San Antonio from October 16 through March 7, 2027.

title: Why Pageant Is Suddenly All the Rage
summary: In a world skewed toward artifice, the East Williamsburg performance space’s commitment to confronting, rather than escaping, one’s conditions in art feels like a renaissance.

title: Tammy Nguyen's New Opera Will Be the Coda to the Venice Biennale
summary: The artist will present an aria from the still-unfinished opera, “Timaeus and The Teacher,” during the festival's closing program.

title: Who’s the Thief in Deana Lawson’s Photography?
summary: I wonder what the women standing perpetually accused and anonymous might say about the sale of their stolen images.

title: Red Hook Open Studios Rises From the Ashes
summary: Dispelling fears that last year's blaze pushed artists away for good, this year's edition proved that the Brooklyn neighborhood’s artistic community is as strong as ever.

title: Richard Dadd’s Strange and Delicate Worlds
summary: Though he is known primarily for his work of fantastical landscapes and mystical woodland creatures, a new retrospective tells the full story.

title: Art Problems: Do I Need an Agent?
summary: Artist agents are not the panacea we imagine them to be, but AI agents won’t solve all your problems, either. Paddy Johnson breaks it down.

title: John Berger in His Own Bruised Time
summary: The late novelist and art critic asked Tom Overton to wait to write his biography until after his death. The result is deeply informative, deferential, and perceptive, sometimes lyrically so.

title: Roy Lichtenstein Was All Style
summary: John Yau on the Whitney’s retrospective of the Pop titan, an interview on Indigenous perseverance with Congress hopeful Jonathan Nez, and art films to see at DOC NYC.

title: NYC Artists Open Their Doors
summary: Open studios and houses, plus reviews of Betty Parsons, Riddikuluz, and the L train burlesque.

title: “Cornell 7” Case Sparks Fury and Protests in Solidarity With Jane Doe
summary: A Nationwide Day of Action on October 8 gathered artists, activists, and survivors in a collective call for institutions to hold abusers accountable.

title: 13 Art Films to See at DOC NYC
summary: Documentaries on a giant pencil that became a local watering hole, the afterlife of Frida Kahlo through her image, and collagist Romare Bearden are among the festival’s most enticing offerings.

title: Sara Flores Paints What the World Stands to Lose
summary: “Every opportunity to show my work is a platform to raise attention on the struggle for self-determination and cultural resistance of the Shipibo people,” the artist told Hyperallergic.

title: Roy Lichtenstein Has Lost His Luster
summary: He went from being a satirist of America’s ideals to a parody of himself, an artist content with other artists’ masterpieces.

title: Utah Groups Sue Trump Administration Over Nine Mile Canyon Construction Project
summary: The environmental organizations filed a suit against the Bureau of Land Management for approving the project that endangers centuries-old Indigenous petroglyphs.
